title: Canary routing bug sends 100% of traffic to a broken new version
source_note: Failure pattern (a release marked as a small canary that a routing/weighting bug actually exposes to all traffic, so a broken build hits everyone) follows the canarying guidance in the Google SRE Workbook. All services, commit hashes, log lines, metrics, and timestamps are fabricated for evaluation.
incident_report: Since ~11:20 UTC checkout-web is throwing 500s for most users. A release went out around 11:18 but it was supposed to be a 1% canary. No infrastructure changes.

signal_lines.msg: canary weight config parsed as 100 (expected 1); routing all checkout-web traffic to 5c6d7e8
unhandled exception in 5c6d7e8 render path: TypeError on null cart total; 500 rate 71%
100% of checkout-web requests served by the canary build; error rate 70%+
canary halted; traffic shifted back to the previous build; errors clearing

deploys.summary: checkout render refactor, released as 1% canary

ground_truth.root_cause: The checkout-web release 5c6d7e8 was meant to receive 1% of traffic as a canary, but the traffic router parsed the canary weight as 100 instead of 1 and routed 100% of checkout-web traffic to the new build. That build has a bug (a TypeError on a null cart total in the render path), so once it was serving everyone the 500 rate jumped to ~71%. The bug would have been caught at 1%; the routing misconfiguration is what made it a full outage.
evidence_path: deploy-system INFO at 11:18: checkout-web 5c6d7e8 released as canary weight=1%
traffic-router WARN: canary weight parsed as 100 (expected 1); all checkout-web traffic routed to 5c6d7e8
checkout-web ERROR: unhandled TypeError in the 5c6d7e8 render path; 5xx rate ~71%
errors clear once traffic is shifted back to the previous build
ground_truth.fix: Halt the canary and shift traffic back (done). Fix the canary-weight parsing in the traffic router and add a guard that rejects a canary weight above a sane ceiling. Separately, fix and re-test the null-cart-total bug before re-releasing.
